jon: Hey team — hitting an annoying one: OTEL span attributes vanish from our app logs when using the py SDK async client + our logging adapter. Minimal repro below, happens reliably when the inference call yields and the task resumes on a different worker thread.

jon: ```python
import asyncio
import logging
from opentelemetry import trace
from redwood import AsyncClient  # pseudocode

logger = logging.getLogger('app')
client = AsyncClient(api_key='x')

async def call_model():
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    logger.info('before call', extra={'span_id': span.get_span_context().span_id})
    await client.generate('hello')
    logger.info('after call', extra={'span_id': trace.get_current_span().get_span_context().span_id})

asyncio.run(call_model())
```

jon: Logs show span ID in the first message but after the await the span context is None (or different). This only happens for async paths that hit our SDK's retry/backoff (so there are internal awaits).

sara: Which versions? otel, sdk, and python?

jon: Python 3.11.6, opentelemetry-api 1.18.0, opentelemetry-sdk 1.18.0, redwood-py 0.9.4. Also tried opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging and it only helps in sync cases.

mike: I've seen context loss across awaits when code uses run_in_executor or when we spawn background tasks without copying context. Two quick angles: (1) ensure the SDK preserves context across internal thread handoffs (use contextvars/context.copy_context when scheduling) and (2) expose a hook so apps can inject logging fields from the current span before/after the request.

jon: Agreed. I tried wrapping our call in copy_context() but the internals of the client do retries + time.sleep in threads and I couldn't intercept. Repro is small but real.

sara: Could we add an optional param to the AsyncClient like `propagate_tracing=True/Callable` that runs a small callback in the same context as the caller before any background schedule? That way we can call logger_adapter.bind_trace(...) without forcing everyone to instrument at app level. :thinking:

mike: Good call. Also typing note: our tracer/callback types are currently Any in the SDK. We should tighten signatures to accept `opentelemetry.trace.Tracer` / `typing.Callable[[opentelemetry.trace.Span], None]` so IDEs catch misuse. Small API bump but low friction.

jon: That would work for us. Also: when SDK does internal retries, it would be ideal if it retained the original span context for logs related to that high-level request (rather than child/blank spans).

mike: I'll open an issue + minimal test. Will propose two PRs: (A) fix internal scheduling to preserve contextvars across any thread handoff, (B) add optional `trace_hook` param + typing and doc examples for logging adapters. Filing now -> github.com/redwood/inference/issues/4217 (placeholder).

jon: Thanks — can you tag this as high priority? It breaks correlation in our observability dashboards for user-facing requests.

ops-bot: Note: related deploys in the last 24h touched the async client (deploy-2026-03-20T21:00Z).

sara: @mike please include a tiny example in the README showing how to preserve span id across retries and an example of `trace_hook` usage. That will unblock platform teams fast.

mike: Will do. I'll ping here when PRs land. :thumbsup:
